title: Brace or splint after an injury
what: An injured arm, leg, or joint is held still so it can heal. A splint, a half cast, or a ready-made brace is used for this.
why: For fractures, hairline cracks, dislocations, bad sprains, or after some surgeries.
duration: putting it on usually takes 10 to 30 minutes; you wear it as long as your doctor says, often a few days to a few weeks
tell_doctor: Where and how you were injured, and when
If the arm or leg is numb, tingling, or pale
Allergy to materials, latex, or tape

prepare.title: Before the visit
prepare.text: Keep the injured area still. You can put something cold on it through a cloth. Do not try to put a joint back in place yourself.

prepare.title: Jewelry
prepare.text: Take rings, bracelets, and watches off the injured arm in advance. With swelling, they are hard to remove.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Loose clothes with a wide sleeve or trouser leg.

bring: X-rays and reports, if you already had them
A ready-made brace, if you bought one as your doctor said
steps: The doctor checks the injury and sends you for an X-ray if needed
The type of support and size are chosen
Soft padding is put on the skin
The splint or brace is put on and secured with a bandage or straps
They check that your fingers or toes are warm, can move, and that nothing is too tight
You are told how to wear it, how to take it off, and when to come back
feel: It may hurt while it is put on, if the injured area is moved
The first days feel strange and awkward. That is normal
The skin may itch under the support
after: Keep the arm or leg raised for the first few days. This reduces swelling
Do not get a plaster splint wet. Take off a brace only if your doctor allows
Do not push anything under the bandage, even if it itches
Come for your checkup and X-ray when your doctor told you
red_flags: Fingers or toes turn blue, pale, or cold: see a doctor urgently
Severe pain that keeps getting worse, numbness, or tingling under the support
The support gets wet, cracks, or presses too hard

faq.q: Can I take the splint off at night?
faq.a: Only if your doctor allows. Most often the splint stays on, or the bone may shift.

faq.q: What can I do if it itches under the splint?
faq.a: Do not push anything under it. Cool air from a hair dryer helps. If the itch is strong, tell your doctor.

reminders.text: Your injury visit is soon. Take rings and bracelets off the injured arm, and bring X-rays, if you have them.
